title: Context Skim Scratchpad — conference crumbs & quick experiments
content:
Topline:
- Short brain-dump after the long-context workshop + reading stack. Trying to stitch the main ideas into small experiments we can run in a day.

Papers / posts I skimmed (quick one-liners):
- "Long-form retrieval as context stitching" (arXiv 2603.01234) — argues for chunk-level KV stitching instead of full prompt concat; claim: cheaper amortized attention for repeated entities.
- "Adaptive KV eviction policies" (conf poster) — tiny policy net decides which KV regions to keep; shows latency win on multi-session workloads.
- "Quantization & context fidelity" blog — low-bit (4-bit) quantization interacts with KV cache precision; hallucination spikes for rare named entities.

Interesting takeaways (things to file away):
- Two axes we need to think about simultaneously: where to store context (KV vs retrieval tokenization) and how to index it for fast prefix-match. Not mutually exclusive.
- Eviction matters more when sessions are long and users flip topics — canonicalizing entity mentions (aliases) reduces cache churn.
- Quantization can be mitigated by keeping critical embeddings/keys at slightly higher precision (hybrid precision). Try 8-bit keys + 4-bit weights.
- Reranking small candidates before KV merge reduces bad prefixes — cheap reranker (distilled) can save expensive decode tokens.

Brainstorm experiment slate (1-day each, cheap compute):
- E1: "alias-canonicalization"
  - dataset: 500 multi-turn customer support threads (internal anonymized).
  - change: map canonical entity ids (customer names, product codes) to canonical tokens before building KV.
  - metric: token-level hallucination probes on targeted QA set + avg latency.

- E2: "hybrid-kv-precision"
  - change: store KV keys at 8-bit (int8) and values at 4-bit in memory-backed cache; on cache miss, fetch full-precision chunk.
  - metric: perplexity on held-out continuation; percent of outputs with OOV entities.

- E3: "micro-rerank-before-merge"
  - pipeline: retrieval -> tiny reranker (2M distilled) -> KV merge -> decode with standard model.
  - metric: top-1 relevance vs baseline, cost delta (ms/token).

Quick notes on implementation gotchas:
- Prefix match speed: naive string compare of tokenized spans is slower than hashed n-gram signatures. Need to benchmark MurmurHash-style signatures at shard-level.
- Concurrency: when multiple requests touch the same session KV, ensure CAS semantics when bumping LRU; otherwise eviction oscillation.
- Memory layout: tightly packing int4 vectors into pages improves GPU memcpy but complicates partial evict. Plan: make eviction operate at chunk granularity (128-token chunks).

Unresolved / researchy questions:
- How bad is quantization drift for rare entity generation exactly? Prior blog shows spikes but not per-entity recall curve. Can we produce per-entity recall vs quant level?
- Is it better to rerank on embedding-space similarity or a tiny cross-attention model pre-merge? Cost vs quality tradeoff unclear.
- For private deployments, what KMS constraints exist if we store canonicalization maps derived from user PII? Need legal check.

Slack / linking notes (to add to PRs and tickets):
- Slack thread: #kv-cache-ops — point to this doc and E2 plan.
- GitHub PR: kv-cache-experiments — branch: hybrid-kv-int8-vals4. Reference this doc in PR description.

Actionable next steps (this week):
- Pick one experiment (E1 preferred) and implement quick preprocessor that maps alias variants to canonical ids. ETA: 1 engineer half-day to wire into existing caching harness.
- Run small chase: 100 sessions, measure latency and hallucination probe.
- If E1 shows >10% hallucination drop for targeted QA, escalate to eng-sre for a canary rollout with LRU bump metrics.

Random notes / quote snippets to remember:
- "Cache fidelity beats cache size for conversational UX." — paraphrase from panel.
- "Quantization should be workload-aware, not model-centric." — developer comment in talk.

TODO (personal):
- [ ] Write a short slide (3 slides) for next sync summarizing E1 plan + sample results.
- [ ] Ping Mika for quick review of the alias-canonicalization mapping rules.
- [ ] Open a Confluence page for long-term experiment logs (link placeholder).

If time allows: try a tiny probe where we inject canonicalized tokens into prompts and measure delta vs KV merge approach — could reveal whether canonicalization alone (no KV changes) gets most of the benefit.

End of scratchpad — shorthand, messy, intentionally incomplete. Will iterate after E1 run.
